summary: Junko Minamoto is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Ryukoku University and Otani University, and held an appointment as a commissioned researcher at Kansai University.

Junmai Zhang worked in philosophy and sinology. He studied under Qichao Liang (~1906–1911) as well as at Waseda University (~1906–1910) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1913–1915), later holding posts at Peking University and Tsinghua University.

Junsho Kato works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Juntaka Kato, Akira Hirakawa, Hajime Nakamura, and Étienne Lamotte, earning a PhD from the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Nishogakusha, Reitaku, and Nagoya universities.

Juntarō Ishihama was a scholar of sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kansai University and held positions at Ryukoku University (~1924–1948) and Kansai University (~1948–1968).
Junzo Inagaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoshin Fukihara and served as section chief at Otani University.
Junzo Tanizawa is a philosophy scholar who served as a researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 1987) and as an associate professor at Shinshu University (attested 2000).

Juri Lotman was a scholar of linguistics and philosophy. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University and its Faculty of Philology (1939–1961) and held a post at the University of Tartu starting in 1954.

Shigeaki Watanabe works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Gerhard Oberhammer and held posts at the University of Tsukuba (attested 1989–1990) and the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2003).
Jushu Nakasone is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as a part-time lecturer at Bukkyo University (attested 2005) and at Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College (attested 2020).

Justin McDaniel is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of California, Riverside, and held an endowed chair at the University of Pennsylvania (attested 2011–2026).

Justin Ritzinger specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under Robert M. Gimello and Michael Puett, later holding posts at Oberlin College, Dharma Drum Mountain, Dharma Drum Institute, and Academia Sinica.
Justin Shimeld is a philosopher who completed his PhD at the University of Tasmania under the supervision of Jeff Malpas and Sonam Thakchoe.
Justus Günther Grassmann studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1797–1801) and held a post at Marienstiftsgymnasium from 1806 to 1852.

Justus Olshausen was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at Kiel, Berlin, and Paris, and held positions at Kiel University, the University of Königsberg, the Prussian Academy of Sciences, and the Prussian ministry.
Jyotirindranath Tagore was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He completed his studies at Hindu School and Presidency University (~1864).

János Szerb was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1974–1980) and held posts at the University of Vienna (1982) and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (1986).

Jérôme Ducor is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Jacques May (~1980–1990) and held posts at the University of Lausanne (~1992) and the International Association of Buddhist Studies (~1999–2011).

Józef Maria Bocheński was a philosopher who studied at Jagiellonian University, the University of Fribourg, and the Pontifical University of Saint Thomas Aquinas. He held posts at the Pontifical University of Saint Thomas Aquinas (~1934–1940) and Fribourg (~1945–1972).

Józef Szczepan Kowalewski worked in linguistics, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Vilnius and Kazan, later serving as professor and rector at Kazan Imperial University (1833–1860) and professor and dean at the University of Warsaw.
Józef Turczyński held posts at the Ukrainian National Academy of Music (~1915–1919) and the Chopin University of Music (~1920–1939).
